pit-crew.flag-yellow-local.comment: A local yellow is shown for an incident ahead — one short warning to slow down and mind the stopped cars. A full-course yellow takes the flag-yellow-full line instead.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-local.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (local). In-sim: drive up to a stopped or spun car in a local yellow sector.

pit-crew.flag-yellow-full.comment: A full-course yellow is out — tells the driver the pace car is being deployed and to close up safely.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-full.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (full). In-sim: a full-course caution in an oval race (the pace car is deployed).

pit-crew.flag-yellow-cleared.comment: A LOCAL yellow has been withdrawn — a short all-clear, replayed after a busier line finishes rather than dropped. It is spoken only for an episode that stayed local, because a local yellow ends with no flag shown at all and this line is the only way the driver learns the sector is clear. A full-course caution ends with a restart instead, and the restart has a line of its own (caution-restart), so no all-clear lands on top of it.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-cleared.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Cleared plays the line on its own. In-sim: clear a local yellow sector. The other half of this line is the SILENCE after a caution — Harness → Flags → Caution → restart replays a full-course caution and restart captured at an oval through the translator; with the race session and hot-lap presets applied it must play the caution sequence through the green-held line and the restart's own "Green, green, green!", with no all-clear behind them.

pit-crew.flag-green.comment: The green flag, when iRacing shows it without its start signal — as at the start of a practice or qualifying session. A race start carries that signal and plays the start lights' go line instead; a caution restart carries it too and plays the caution restart line. The wording differs per session type (practice, qualifying, race), so it branches on session.type; an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-green.test: Harness → Flags → Green, after choosing a session preset (practice, qualifying or race). In-sim: the green at the start of a practice or qualifying session. Not at a race start ("Go, go, go!") nor at a caution restart (its own "Green, green, green!").

pit-crew.flag-blue.comment: A faster car is about to lap the driver — asks for mirrors and a clean pass.
pit-crew.flag-blue.test: Harness → Flags → Blue. In-sim: get shown the blue flag as a lapping car closes in.

pit-crew.flag-white.comment: The white flag — the leader's final lap in a race, or the last lap of a practice or qualifying session; the wording follows session.type, and an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-white.test: Harness → Flags → White, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: the white flag comes out on the leader's final lap (race) or on your own last lap (practice, qualifying).

pit-crew.flag-white-last-lap.comment: The driver has crossed the line under the white flag and started their own last lap — give it everything. Race-only; stage two of the white-flag call.
pit-crew.flag-white-last-lap.test: Harness → Flags → White — Last Lap Started, with the race session preset. In-sim: cross start/finish while the white flag flies in a race.

pit-crew.flag-white-leader.comment: The overall leader has started their final lap while the driver is still some way behind — a heads-up that the race is about to end.
pit-crew.flag-white-leader.test: Harness → Flags → Leader's final lap, with the race session preset. In-sim: in a race, let the leader take the white flag while you are a lap or more down.

pit-crew.flag-red.comment: The red flag — the session is stopped; tells the driver to slow down and drive carefully back to the pits.
pit-crew.flag-red.test: Harness → Flags → Red. In-sim: a red flag in a hosted or league session.

pit-crew.flag-black.comment: A black flag has been issued — the driver has a penalty to serve within three laps.
pit-crew.flag-black.test: Harness → Flags → Black. In-sim: speed in the pit lane, or ignore a furled black flag; a race admin can also issue one (!black).

pit-crew.flag-checkered.comment: The checkered flag — the session is over. The wording follows session.type (the well-done only after a race); an unknown session type takes the race line.
pit-crew.flag-checkered.test: Harness → Flags → Checkered, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: take the checkered flag at the end of any session.

pit-crew.flag-debris.comment: A debris flag — something is on the track ahead; asks the driver to be careful.
pit-crew.flag-debris.test: Harness → Flags → Debris. In-sim: the debris flag after an incident leaves parts on the track.

pit-crew.flag-meatball.comment: The meatball flag — mandatory repairs, the driver must pit. Cuts any other line in flight and is never dropped.
pit-crew.flag-meatball.test: Harness → Flags → Meatball. In-sim: take enough damage that iRacing orders you in for repairs.

pit-crew.flag-disqualify.comment: The driver has been disqualified — pull off the track.
pit-crew.flag-disqualify.test: Harness → Flags → Disqualify. In-sim: exceed the session's incident limit, or a race admin disqualifies you (!dq).

pit-crew.flag-furled.comment: The furled black flag — the driver gained time and must give it back.
pit-crew.flag-furled.test: Harness → Flags → Furled. In-sim: cut a corner and gain time; the furled flag shows until the time is given back.

pit-crew.flag-furled-cleared.comment: The furled warning has been withdrawn after the driver gave the time back.
pit-crew.flag-furled-cleared.test: Harness → Flags → Furled, then Harness → Flags → Furled Cleared. In-sim: give the time back after a furled black flag.

pit-crew.flag-dq-scoring-invalid.comment: The driver has been disqualified and their scoring invalidated — DQ, scoring's off.
pit-crew.flag-dq-scoring-invalid.test: Harness → Flags → DQ — Scoring Invalid. In-sim: a disqualification that also invalidates scoring (rare; the harness is the practical route).

pit-crew.flag-crossed.comment: Crossed flags — the halfway point of the race. Race-only, while the driver is live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-crossed.test: Harness → Flags → Crossed, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: reach the halfway point of an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-one-pace-lap-to-go.comment: One lap to green on a rolling start that runs two pace laps — the caution's one-lap-to-green sentence, from the same clips, with the formation lineup read from the pace rows at the moment it is spoken. On pole: "One lap to green. You're leading them away." On the front row with only the pace car ahead but not on pole — the outside car of a double-file formation — a plain "One lap to green." Otherwise the lane and the car ahead: inside or outside on an oval running double file, and "Line up behind" with no lane anywhere else or single file. With no lineup to read, or a car ahead the session cannot name, the plain "One lap to green." too — this call must never come out as nothing, so it asks rollingStart.hasFollowCarNumber before choosing a numbered wording rather than leaving the number to an optional clause alone. A one-lap formation has no such moment and never hears it. Race-only and live in the car; it waits behind a line in progress, and stays unsaid once the formation is over.
pit-crew.flag-one-pace-lap-to-go.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Rolling Start → Formation (oval, two laps), with the race session preset on an oval — expect it as the pace car completes its first lap, with the lane and the car ahead; Harness → Flags → One Lap to Green fires the event alone, and speaks only while a formation is running. In-sim: the last pace lap of a rolling start that runs two pace laps.

pit-crew.flag-green-held.comment: The green is imminent — get ready to launch. The flag rises several seconds before the pace car leaves, so no line here says where the pace car is; caution/pace-car-off does that at its real exit. Rolling starts and restarts only; a standing-start grid is the start lights' business.
pit-crew.flag-green-held.test: Harness → Flags → Green Held, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: the final pace lap of a rolling start or restart, several seconds before the pace car leaves the track.

pit-crew.flag-ten-to-go.comment: Ten laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-ten-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → Ten to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: ten laps remaining in an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-five-to-go.comment: Five laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
pit-crew.flag-five-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → Five to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: five laps remaining in an oval race.

pit-crew.flag-yellow-waving.comment: A waving yellow — a fresh incident right ahead, more urgent than the standing yellow. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds while the incident persists.
pit-crew.flag-yellow-waving.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Waving. In-sim: approach a sector where a car has just crashed or spun.

pit-crew.flag-caution-waving.comment: The caution is out — one of three wordings, none of them promising the pace car, which the caution-pace-car-out line reports when it actually arrives. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds, and waits behind a line in progress rather than being dropped.
pit-crew.flag-caution-waving.test: Harness → Flags → Caution Waving; Harness → Flags → Caution → restart hears it first, with the follow line behind it. In-sim: the caution comes out in a race as the field bunches up.

pit-crew.caution-follow.comment: Who to line up behind, a couple of seconds after the caution announcement, read from the pace rows at the moment it is spoken. With nobody ahead in your own line it is the pace car — "You're leading them — it's just you and the pace car." — and otherwise "Line up behind" and the number — a clip of its own that says "car" and the number, spoken the way the sim spells it. A car ahead the session cannot name gets "Line up behind the car ahead." instead: the lead-in and the number are one optional clause, and an optional clause alone expands to nothing, so the call asks caution.hasFollowCarNumber first rather than leave the driver with no instruction at all.
pit-crew.caution-follow.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart (or Caution → lineup change, Caution → extra lap), with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect "…behind car eight" about two and a half seconds after the caution line; with the practice preset (a player car but an empty driver list) the car ahead cannot be named, so expect "Line up behind the car ahead." In-sim: a full-course caution in a race, from anywhere but the lead.

pit-crew.caution-pace-car-out.comment: The pace car has reached the track — one short heads-up, in one of three wordings.
pit-crew.caution-pace-car-out.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets, hears it a few seconds after the follow line; or inject paceCar.deployed while a caution is out. In-sim: about twenty seconds after the caution comes out in a race.

pit-crew.caution-field-caught.comment: Two to green — the pace car has finished its pickup lap, which on an oval is one leader crossing before the one-to-go flag. "Two to green." always speaks; then, only with a car ahead in your own line, an optional clause naming it ("Make sure to follow" and the number — with the pace car the only thing ahead the clause is left out). No position here: that moved to pit-crew.caution-position, on the last lap. The optional clause is safe because the sentence outside it always speaks — the rule an optional clause has to meet. On a road course the contract keeps this silent (one to green rises on the same tick there), so the pack never chooses.
pit-crew.caution-field-caught.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect "Two to green." and "…follow car eight" a few seconds after the pace-car line. In-sim: the waving caution goes static as the pace car gathers the field, about a lap and a half in, on an oval.

pit-crew.caution-extra-lap.comment: The caution has been extended past the two laps it defaults to — one of three ways of saying the field is going around again. Never a lap count: nothing in the sim says how many are left, so each extra lap is reported as it happens.
pit-crew.caution-extra-lap.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → extra lap, with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect it after the leader's extra crossing, before the one-lap-to-green line. In-sim: an admin adds a pace lap (!pacelaps +1) after the pickup.

pit-crew.caution-one-to-go.comment: One lap to green, with the restart lineup. Leading: "One lap to green. You're leading them away." On the front row with only the pace car ahead but not the leader — the outside car of a double-file restart — a plain "One lap to green.", since telling P2 it leads would be wrong. Otherwise the lane and the car ahead, read from the pace rows at speak time: inside or outside on an oval running double file, and "Line up behind" with no lane anywhere else or single file. A car ahead the session cannot name gets the plain "One lap to green." too — this is the one call that must never come out as nothing, so it asks caution.hasFollowCarNumber before choosing a numbered wording rather than leaving the number to an optional clause alone, which expands to silence when there is no number to say. The numbered wordings already contain the words "One lap to green", which is why the fallback replaces them rather than preceding them.
pit-crew.caution-one-to-go.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets — a double-file lineup, so expect "One lap to green. … behind car eight", with the lane when the preset's track is an oval; Caution → lineup change re-forms single file and hears the plain wording. With no session preset the run is refused, and with the practice preset (a player car but an empty driver list) the car ahead cannot be named, so expect the bare "One lap to green." In-sim: the one-to-go flag on the last caution lap.

pit-crew.caution-lineup-changed.comment: The car you line up behind changed mid-caution — someone pitted, or the field re-formed. "Change —" then, with only the pace car ahead now, "you're at the front now, just the pace car ahead"; otherwise the lane and the new car ahead, in the same three shapes as the one-lap-to-green line (inside, outside, or no lane), each an optional clause with its number. A new car ahead the session cannot name gets "The car ahead of you has changed." — asked through caution.hasFollowCarNumber before the lane is chosen, because an optional clause alone expands to nothing. That fallback deliberately drops the lane even where caution.line would answer: four more clips to keep it on a rare path is not proportionate.
pit-crew.caution-lineup-changed.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → lineup change, with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect "Change — you're behind car seven" a second and a half after the reorder; with the practice preset (a player car but an empty driver list) the new car ahead cannot be named, so expect "The car ahead of you has changed." In-sim: pit under caution, or a car ahead of you pitting, before the one-to-go flag.

pit-crew.caution-catch-up.comment: You have dropped back from the car you line up behind under caution — close the gap. With only the pace car ahead in your own line, "Close up on the pace car." or "You've dropped off the pace car. Close it up."; otherwise one of three lead-ins — "Close it up. Catch", "Gap's opened. Close up on", "You've dropped back. Catch up to" — and the number of the car ahead, a clip of its own that says "car" and the number, spoken the way the sim spells it. No lane: the lane has not changed, and this call is about distance. A car ahead the session cannot name gets "Close the gap to the car ahead." or "You've dropped back. Close it up." instead: the lead-in and the number are one optional clause, and an optional clause alone expands to nothing, so the call asks caution.hasFollowCarNumber first. Whether the gap is open is the translator's decision and the contract's speak-time check, never the script's — a call that waited for the bus is dropped once you have closed up.
pit-crew.caution-catch-up.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → catch-up, with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect "Close it up. Catch car …" a few seconds after the gap to the car ahead opens. In-sim: under a full-course caution, once the field has formed up behind the pace car, lift and let the car ahead of you in your line pull well away.

pit-crew.caution-catch-up-reminder.comment: The gap to the car ahead under caution is still open and you are not closing it — the catch-up call again, in other words. With a car ahead the session can name, "Still a gap. Close up on" or "Keep closing. You're still off the back of" and its number; with only the pace car ahead, or a car the session cannot name, the lines the first call uses there. At most two reminders for one gap, thirty seconds apart, and none after a pit stop — the translator's count, not the script's. A reminder that finds the bus busy is dropped rather than queued: the next one replaces it.
pit-crew.caution-catch-up-reminder.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → catch-up, with the race session and hot-lap presets — the button holds the gap open, so expect "Still a gap. Close up on car …" thirty seconds after the first call. In-sim: stay well back from the car ahead for half a minute after the first catch-up call, without closing.

pit-crew.caution-position.comment: Your race position, about a third of the way into the last caution lap — the normal position wording ("We're currently" and the number). The number is caution.racePosition, the live race position at the moment it is spoken, NOT caution.restartPosition: a lapped car lined up ahead of you is behind you in the race, and the number your display shows is the race one (a 2026-09-19 test heard "P21" in a 20-car field from the lineup, with the display on P19). The WHOLE call is one optional clause, and here that is correct rather than the empty-sequence defect the other caution entries guard against: a position call with no position — no running order to read, or a field past the spoken range — has nothing true to say, so saying nothing IS the right sentence. Do not add a fallback wording outside the clause.
pit-crew.caution-position.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets — expect "We're currently seven" a couple of seconds after the one-lap-to-green line (the button patches per-car lap progress at one to go so the race order can rank you; the hot-lap preset alone carries none). In-sim: about 35% into the one-lap-to-green lap; a lapped car lined up ahead of you does not count.

pit-crew.caution-pace-car-off.comment: The pace car is peeling off — the green is seconds away.
pit-crew.caution-pace-car-off.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets, hears it a few seconds before the restart line; or inject paceCar.off while a caution is out. In-sim: the pace car heads for pit road on the last caution lap, or at an opening rolling start once the green is held.

pit-crew.caution-restart.comment: The green that ends the caution — "Green, green, green! Go, go, go!" or a shorter variant. Its own line rather than the race start's go line, and it cuts anything still playing.
pit-crew.caution-restart.test: Harness → Flags → Caution → restart, with the race session and hot-lap presets — the last thing heard. In-sim: the green at a caution restart in a race.

pit-crew.pit-readback-entry.comment: Reads back the queued pit service as the car enters the pit lane, and again — without the opener — after the driver changes the queue while still on pit road. A limiter reminder leads on the initial entry when the car has one and it is off; nothing queued collapses the whole recap to the empty-fallback line.
pit-crew.pit-readback-entry.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to entry (entry-refire for the mid-lane replay) after setting a service snapshot with the Fuel Queued, Tires LF/RF/LR/RR (or the All / Fronts / Rears / Lefts / Rights / None presets), Compound, Fast Repair Queued / Available and Windshield Queued controls; leave Limiter Engaged unchecked for the pre-opener, and set damage on the Engine Warnings panel for the fast-repair slot. In-sim: queue fuel and two tires, then enter the pit lane.

pit-crew.pit-readback-exit.comment: Confirms the queued pit service a few seconds after the car leaves the pit lane — the same recap under a "to confirm" opener, which stays even when nothing is queued so the empty-fallback line still reads as a confirmation.
pit-crew.pit-readback-exit.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to exit after setting a service snapshot with the same controls. In-sim: queue a service, drive through the pits and out; the confirmation follows the pit-lane exit.

pit-crew.tire-wear-report.comment: After a pit stop, once the exit readback has played: the remaining tread of all four tires, front to rear, each as the lowest of its three zones in whole percent, then where the wear is heaviest, a sentence left out when every tire still reads one hundred. After a tire change the numbers describe the set that came off.
pit-crew.tire-wear-report.test: Harness → Tire Wear → Report after a stop. In-sim: drive into your box, stop, and leave pit road; the report follows the exit readback.

pit-crew.readout-fuel-last-lap.comment: On a Session Info key press: the fuel the last clean lap used, rounded to a tenth, in the driver's display unit — "Fuel used last lap, two point four liters." The tenths clip carries the unit.

pit-crew.readout-track-temp.comment: On a Session Info key press: the track temperature as a whole number — "Track temperature is forty one degrees." The unit is not named, as in the session-start brief; a pack that records the unit clips can add {{readout.degreesUnit}}.
pit-crew.readout-track-temp.test: Harness → Telemetry Readout → Track temperature (°C). In-sim: add a Session Info key on Track Temperature and press it on track.

pit-crew.rolling-start-pace-car.comment: The pace car has started moving the field onto the formation lap of a rolling start, and who you form up behind, read from the pace rows at the moment it is spoken. On pole: "Pace car's rolling. You're on pole. Just you and the pace car." With only the pace car ahead in your own line but not leading — typically the outside car of a double-file front row — "Pace car's rolling. Nothing ahead of you but the pace car.", since that car is not on pole and nothing establishes its row. Otherwise the lane and the car ahead: "Inside line, behind" or "Outside line, behind" on an oval running double file, "Form up behind" with no lane anywhere else or single file, and then the number — a clip of its own that says "car" and the number, spoken the way the sim spells it. With no lineup to read, or a car ahead the session cannot name, one of the five numberless lines ("…get moving and follow the car ahead."): the call asks rollingStart.hasFollowCarNumber before choosing a numbered wording, because the lead-in and the number are one optional clause and an optional clause alone expands to nothing. Race-only and live in the car; it waits behind a line in progress rather than being dropped, and stays unsaid once the formation is over.
pit-crew.rolling-start-pace-car.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Rolling Start → Formation (oval, two laps), with the race session preset on an oval — expect "Pace car's rolling" with the lane and "behind car …" as the field rolls; Rolling Start → Pace car moving fires the event alone, and speaks only while a formation is running. In-sim: sit on the grid of a rolling-start race and wait for the pace car to pull away.

pit-crew.rolling-start-lineup-changed.comment: The car you form up behind changed during a rolling-start formation — a car ahead dropped out, or was passed. The caution's change line, from the same clips: "Change —" then, with only the pace car ahead now, "you're at the front now, just the pace car ahead"; otherwise the lane and the new car ahead, in three shapes (inside, outside, or no lane), each an optional clause with its number. A new car ahead the session cannot name gets "The car ahead of you has changed." — asked through rollingStart.hasFollowCarNumber before the lane is chosen, because an optional clause alone expands to nothing. The contract keeps it silent when the car ahead is the one the engineer last named in this formation, once you hold no pace row, and once the formation is over, so the pack never chooses.
pit-crew.rolling-start-lineup-changed.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Rolling Start → Formation (oval, two laps), with the race session preset on an oval — expect "Change — you're on the inside behind car …" a second and a half after the car ahead of you drops out; Rolling Start → Car ahead changed fires the event alone, and speaks only while a formation is running and the car ahead is not the one last named. pit-crew.limiter-dropped.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter dropped. In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, disengage it while still on pit road.

pit-crew.limiter-speeding.comment: The car is over the pit speed limit on a car that has a limiter — the fix is to press the button, which is why this line is separate from the no-limiter one.
pit-crew.limiter-speeding.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Speeding (limiter car). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

pit-crew.start-light-ready.comment: The start gantry has lit — lights are up, the standing start is seconds away. Critical and interrupting, and replayed rather than lost if a spotter call holds the bus; a later go line replaces it if it never got out.
pit-crew.start-light-ready.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Ready, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: the red lights come on for a standing start.

pit-crew.start-light-go.comment: Go, go, go — the moment iRacing releases the field: lights out at a standing start, or the green at a rolling start. A caution restart has its own line (caution-restart). Critical and interrupting: it cuts anything in flight, including a ready line still playing.
pit-crew.start-light-go.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Go, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: the lights go out at a standing start, or the field is released at a rolling start.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-90.comment: Ninety seconds to the start — the first get-in-the-car reminder, spoken from the garage or session screen too. Ordinary weight, and dropped rather than replayed stale if the bus is busy.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-90.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 90, with the race session preset. In-sim: sit in the garage as a standing-start race counts down.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-60.comment: Sixty seconds to the start — the same reminder, one mark closer.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-60.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 60, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes sixty seconds.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-30.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 30, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes thirty seconds.

pit-crew.start-light-countdown-10.comment: Ten seconds to the start — the last mark before the gantry lights.
pit-crew.start-light-countdown-10.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 10, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes ten seconds.

pit-crew.incident-off-track.comment: The driver ran off track — a short coaching line about track limits, with no point count (the type has none worth stating). A faster, worse incident in the same crash replaces this line mid-sentence.
pit-crew.incident-off-track.test: Harness → Incidents → Off Track (1x). In-sim: put four wheels off in any session.

pit-crew.incident-out-of-control.comment: The driver lost control of the car (a spin) — a calm-down line, no point count.
pit-crew.incident-out-of-control.test: Harness → Incidents → Out of Control (2x). In-sim: spin the car.

pit-crew.incident-contact-world.comment: Light contact with the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as a separate clause. The count is optional because it is a whole sentence of its own — a light touch worth no points, or a count the voice has no clip for, leaves the type line standing on its own.
pit-crew.incident-contact-world.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Wall (0x) (the type line alone) or Collision — Wall (2x) for a count. In-sim: brush a wall lightly.

pit-crew.incident-collision-world.comment: A hard hit on the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause.
pit-crew.incident-collision-world.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Wall (2x). In-sim: hit a wall hard.

pit-crew.incident-contact-car.comment: Light contact with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — nothing when the rub cost none.
pit-crew.incident-contact-car.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Car (0x). In-sim: rub doors with another car.

pit-crew.incident-collision-car.comment: A heavy collision with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — four on pavement, two on dirt, whatever the sim scored, and nothing for a count the voice cannot say.
pit-crew.incident-collision-car.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Car (4x), Collision — Car (2x, dirt) or Collision — Car (escalated). In-sim: a hard collision with another car.

pit-crew.no-limiter-speeding.comment: Over the pit speed limit on a car that has NO pit limiter — the fix is to lift, so this line must never mention a limiter. The mirror of limiter-speeding; exactly one of the two speaks to any car.
pit-crew.no-limiter-speeding.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Speeding (no limiter). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

pit-crew.no-limiter-entry.comment: Pit entry on a car with no limiter: a reminder to mind the limit, then the limit itself — intro, number, unit — as one optional clause. The number is the whole point of the clause and a fragment of its sentence, so a limit the voice has no clip for drops the clause entirely rather than speaking the intro into silence; the reminder still stands alone as a complete sentence.
pit-crew.no-limiter-entry.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Pit entry reminder, after Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start with the Pit speed limit set (the limit clause reads that snapshot; without one only the reminder plays). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, enter pit road.

pit-crew.lap-time-best.comment: A new session-best lap, or the driver's first valid lap: the intro (best-lap-yet or first-good-lap), then the lap time to the thousandth read as whole phrases, the way every lap is read, the minute and seconds as one clip and the thousandths as another (one twenty three, point four five six). Both halves are required, because a time missing either is not a time; a lap the voice has no clock clip for, eleven minutes and up, drops the whole line.
pit-crew.lap-time-best.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Lap Time → Best Lap 1:23.456 (Best Lap 0:34.812 for a lap under a minute, First Valid Lap 2:07.007 for the other intro). In-sim: set a personal best in any session, or complete the first clean lap of a session.

pit-crew.gap-trend.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor has turned: we are gaining on the car ahead, it is pulling away, the car behind is gaining, or we are dropping it. The line is chosen by side and direction; the live gap readout follows through the gap-readout fragment. Both gap lines share one cooldown (30 s by default), so a second one inside it stays silent.
pit-crew.gap-trend.test: Harness → Gaps → Trend: closing on car ahead, Trend: car ahead pulling away, Trend: car behind gaining or Trend: dropping the car behind — the seconds clause needs a live gap, so drive the harness session with cars around you. In-sim: race with a car a few seconds ahead and close on it lap after lap.

pit-crew.gap-threshold.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor first dropped under the driver's alert threshold — we have caught the car ahead, or the car behind is right with us — then the live gap through the same gap-readout fragment. Shares the trend line's cooldown.
pit-crew.gap-threshold.test: Harness → Gaps → Caught the car ahead (threshold) or Car behind within threshold, with a live gap for the seconds clause. In-sim: close to within the configured gap threshold of the car ahead.

pit-crew.race-status.comment: The every-three-laps status update while the driver holds position in a race: the leader hears the whole still-leading line (still leading our class in a multi-class race), everyone else hears "we're currently" and the live position. Both branches are read at speak time, so a deferred update is never stale. The number is part of the sentence and stays required.
pit-crew.race-status.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Status update (P5 on lap 7) or Leader status (P1 on lap 6) — both are MUTE in the harness, which has no live position for the readout to speak, so only the fire attempt shows in the log. In-sim: hold the same race position for three consecutive laps after the green; the update comes as you cross the line on the third.

pit-crew.toggle-fuel-on.comment: The driver queued fuel for the next stop — a short acknowledgment (got it / roger that / copy that) then the confirmation, the shape every toggle confirmation in this family shares. The acknowledgment is pit-actions/acknowledgment, a different pool from the generic acknowledgment/acknowledgment: a smaller set tuned for this register, with its own no-repeat tracker by virtue of being a different group and base, so no named pool is needed for the two to stay independent. Silent for a few seconds after leaving the pit lane, when the sim resets the queue on its own.
pit-crew.toggle-fuel-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel ON, not within about 4.5 s of Exited Pit Lane (the pit-action cooldown). In-sim: press the fuel toggle in the pit black box, or on a Fuel Service key.

pit-crew.toggle-fuel-off.comment: The driver removed fuel from the next stop — acknowledgment, then the confirmation.
pit-crew.toggle-fuel-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fuel toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.auto-fuel-on-refuel.comment: Autofuel was switched on and the fuel request is left set, so the line says both — autofuel is on, and we are refueling. The bare line, with no acknowledgment in front: the missing "Got it." is what marks an autofuel change rather than a request the engineer is answering. A fuel-bit flip while autofuel is armed says nothing at all, so these four lines are the only fuel news in that window. It shares the manual fuel toggle's family, so a newer fuel line replaces it rather than stacking behind it, and like the toggle confirmations it stays silent for a few seconds after leaving the pit lane.
pit-crew.auto-fuel-on-refuel.test: Harness → Pit Service → Autofuel ON, refueling, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch autofuel on in the pit black box; this is the line when the fuel request is left set.

pit-crew.auto-fuel-on-no-refuel.comment: Autofuel was switched on and the fuel request is left clear — switching it on can wipe one the driver had queued, which is what the sim did on the pit approach in the #474 capture. The bare line, no acknowledgment, as for the three siblings.
pit-crew.auto-fuel-on-no-refuel.test: Harness → Pit Service → Autofuel ON, no fuel, outside the pit-action cooldown; Harness → Pit Service → Autofuel takeover (replay) drives the captured pit-approach moment through the translator. In-sim: switch autofuel on in the pit black box; this is the line when the request is left clear.

pit-crew.auto-fuel-off-refuel.comment: Autofuel was switched off and the fuel request it had set is still standing, so the stop still takes fuel — the case that is easy to miss, since switching autofuel off looks like cancelling the fueling and does not. The bare line, no acknowledgment, as for the three siblings.
pit-crew.auto-fuel-off-refuel.test: Harness → Pit Service → Autofuel OFF, still refueling, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: with autofuel on and fueling, switch autofuel off — the ordinary fuel request stays set.

pit-crew.auto-fuel-off-no-refuel.comment: Autofuel was switched off with no fuel request left behind, so nothing goes in at the next stop. The bare line, no acknowledgment, as for the three siblings.
pit-crew.auto-fuel-off-no-refuel.test: Harness → Pit Service → Autofuel OFF, no fuel, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: with no fuel queued, switch autofuel off in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-all.comment: All four tires queued — acknowledgment, then the confirmation. Each tire line answers the RESULTING set, whichever buttons got the driver there.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-all.test: Harness → Tire Service → All, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all four tires in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-fronts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Fronts, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the front tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rears.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rears, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the rear tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lefts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Lefts, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the left-side tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rights.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rights, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-side tires only.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lf.comment: The left-front only — a puncture-style single change.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-lf.test: Harness → Tire Service → LF only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the left-front tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rf.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the right-front tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → LR only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the left-rear tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rr.test: Harness → Tire Service → RR only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the right-rear tire.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-lf-rr.test: Harness → Tire Service → LF + RR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the left-front and right-rear tires.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-rf-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF + LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-front and left-rear tires.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rr.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-rear.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rr.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-rear.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lr.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-rear.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lr.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-rear.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rf.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-front.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-rf.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-front.

pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lf.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-front.
pit-crew.tire-set-on-skip-lf.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-front.

pit-crew.tire-set-off.comment: Every tire cleared from the next stop — spoken only when the resulting set is empty, never on a side-switch that merely removes some tires.
pit-crew.tire-set-off.test: Harness → Tire Service → Skip, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear every tire in the pit black box.

pit-crew.tire-compound-dry.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to dry. The one confirmation for the switch — the all-four-tires event iRacing raises alongside it is suppressed before it reaches the engineer.
pit-crew.tire-compound-dry.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → DRY, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to dry.

pit-crew.tire-compound-wet.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to wet.
pit-crew.tire-compound-wet.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → WET, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to wet.

pit-crew.toggle-windshield-on.comment: A windshield clean queued for the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-windshield-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-windshield-off.comment: The windshield clean removed from the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-windshield-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-on.comment: A fast repair queued for the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-on.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-off.comment: The fast repair removed from the next stop.
pit-crew.toggle-fast-repair-off.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

pit-crew.overtake-gained-position.comment: The position readout after a gained overtake — "We're currently", then the live position — played once the reaction line has finished. It is skipped for a podium gain, whose reaction line already states the place, and never doubles a position announced by another line in the last 20 seconds. The lead-in is an optional clause: a second readout within 30 seconds that moved at most one place says the bare number ("P four"), which is a complete, true statement on its own; a script that always wants the lead-in drops the optional.
pit-crew.overtake-gained-position.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes buttons fire the reaction but the harness has no live position, so this readout has nothing to say there. In-sim: pass a car in a race outside the top three; the reaction (when it rolls) is followed by the current position, and a second pass within half a minute reads the bare number.

pit-crew.overtake-lost-position.comment: The position readout after a lost place — the same lead-in and live number as the gained readout, under the same 20-second no-double rule and the same optional lead-in.
pit-crew.overtake-lost-position.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes → Lost — now P5 button fires the reaction but the harness has no live position for this readout. In-sim: get passed in a race; the come-on line (when it rolls) is followed by the current position.

pit-crew.race-end.comment: The final result as the driver crosses the line after the checkered: the driver's name, then one line per result — we won, second place, the podium in third, or the race-is-over line with the position number for fourth or worse. The greeting is optional because names are a union across voices and the result reads whole without it; the position number is part of the last line and stays required. Deferred behind a same-lap best-lap readout rather than cutting it — the race is over either way.
pit-crew.race-end.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Race over — P1 (we won!), or Race over — P2 (second place), Race over — P3 (podium) and Race over — P9 (mid-pack) for the other branches, Race over — multi-class P15 / class P1 for a class win. In-sim: take the checkered flag in a race and cross the line.

pit-crew.position-change.comment: The driver's position after a completed lap, in one of three shapes: a qualifying lap the sim did not count says "That lap didn't count", then "We're currently" and the position when there is one (on a first lap there is none, and the first sentence plays alone); a lap that put the driver on pole says the pole line alone; every other lap says the intro ("That puts us to" for a gain in qualifying, "We're currently" otherwise, and always in a race) and the position, read live in a race. Practice stays silent, and a race hold is left to the race-status update.
pit-crew.position-change.test: Harness → Position → Improved 5 → 3, Worsened 3 → 5, First Valid Lap P1, Qualifying P1 (pole), Holding P1 (qualifying, slow lap), Unchanged P5 (non-PB lap) or the Invalid lap, … buttons (all qualifying). The race branch is mute in the harness (no live position) — In-sim: complete a race lap having gained or lost a place.

pit-crew.overtake-gained.comment: The reaction to a gained overtake, one line chosen by what the pass earned: the lead (overall, or in class in a multi-class race), second or third place — each of those states the position itself, so no readout follows — or the plain "Nice pass" for anything else, which the separate position readout then completes. A podium pass always reacts; any other pass reacts about one time in three, and a place gained because a car ahead retired never does.
pit-crew.overtake-gained.test: Harness → Overtakes → Gained — now P5 (nice pass), Gained the lead (P2 → P1), Gained — multi-class (class P3 → P2), Gained — P3 → P2 (podium line), Gained — P4 → P3 (podium line); Gained — retirement (readout only) stays silent here. In-sim: pass a car cleanly in a race.

pit-crew.overtake-lost.comment: The reaction to a lost place: "Come on, <name>." in the driver's chosen name, then "Don't give up positions like that." The opener is a complete sentence of its own and is optional — a voice without a clip for the chosen name skips it and the line still plays. A lost podium place always reacts; any other loss about one time in three.
pit-crew.overtake-lost.test: Harness → Overtakes → Lost — now P5. In-sim: get passed in a race.

pit-crew.qualifying-invalidation-lap-inv.comment: An incident on a counted qualifying lap: the invalidated line always, then — only in lap-limited qualifying, where a count means something — a tail for how many counted laps remain: out of laps, one to five by count (each a whole sentence with its own encouragement), or plenty above five. The tail is a whole clause, so an if with no else is right for it; a count the case has no key for says nothing. One callout per lap however many incidents; silent on out-laps and beyond the counted attempts.
pit-crew.qualifying-invalidation-lap-inv.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Qualifying Invalidation → Off-Track — 3 laps left (Contact-Car — 1 lap left, Off-Track — out of laps, Off-Track — plenty of laps, Off-Track — time-limited for the other tails; the four (silent) buttons and Same Lap Again (latch) for the suppressions). In-sim: go off track on a flying lap of a lap-limited qualifying session.

pit-crew.race-start.comment: The grid brief a few seconds into a race session: the driver's name, the starting position (from pole, or qualifying put us to P N), the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a qualifying one. Every clause is optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without — a name, a position number or a temperature the voice cannot say, or iRacing has not reported yet, drops its own clause and nothing else; the position branch is a case inside its clause so a pack can rephrase pole and composed apart. The wetness branches on whether iRacing has reported it: known, it is read out; still unknown when the brief speaks, the engineer says so rather than leaving the track unmentioned.
pit-crew.race-start.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race Start → Race start — P5, with the race session preset (Race start — P1 (pole), Race start — P65 (out of range) and Race start — no position for the other position branches; the setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: load a setup whose name matches the qualifying pattern under Setup Warning Patterns). In-sim: sit through the transition into a race session; the brief comes a few seconds in, once iRacing reports the track conditions, and at most ten seconds in.

pit-crew.session-start.comment: The brief a few seconds into a practice or qualifying session (a race takes the race-start brief instead): the driver's name, which session it is, the pit speed limit with its unit, the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and — in qualifying only — a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a race one. The greeting, the pit-speed limit, both temperatures and the nudge are optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without: a name, a limit or a temperature the voice cannot say, or iRacing has not reported yet, drops its own clause and nothing else. The wetness branches on whether iRacing has reported it: known, it is read out; still unknown when the brief speaks, the engineer says so rather than leaving the track unmentioned. The session line is required — a brief that names no session is not a brief.
pit-crew.session-start.test: Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start, with Session type set to practice or qualifying (race is silent here — it is the race-start callout's); Fire as Fresh Connect covers the mid-session connect; set Track wetness to Unknown (or empty a temperature) to hear the brief go ahead without it after its ten-second wait. The setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: in qualifying, load a setup whose name matches the race pattern under Setup Warning Patterns. In-sim: join a practice or qualifying session; the brief comes a few seconds after the session begins, once iRacing reports the track conditions and at most ten seconds in, in the garage or on track.

pit-crew.spotter-call.comment: A spotter transition call — a car has appeared alongside, a second one joined it, one of two has gone, or the sides swapped: "Car left", "Two cars right", "Three wide", "Clear right, car left", with inside/outside terms on an oval. The spotter engine picks the clip for the exact transition and hands it over as the spotterClip var, so the call is that one step; it cuts anything in flight and is never replayed late. No radio frame: the beeps would drown a call that has to land at once.
pit-crew.spotter-call.test: Harness → Radar → Left, Right, Both Sides, Two Left, Two Right (each from the state the button names). In-sim: let a car pull alongside in any session with the spotter enabled.

pit-crew.spotter-info.comment: The spotter's informational lines — "Clear" once the car alongside has genuinely separated, and the still-there reminder ("Still there", "Hold your line") on its cadence while a car stays alongside. The same engine-picked spotterClip step as the call, at a lower weight so a reminder can never chop a critical line. No radio frame.
pit-crew.spotter-info.test: Harness → Radar → Clear (after Left or Right); the still-there reminder repeats on its own while a side stays occupied. In-sim: hold a car alongside for a few seconds, then let it go.

pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-right-behind.comment: Stopped or crawling on track with the nearest car under two seconds away: a whole line from a pool of four, such as "Car right behind you. Watch out." or "Right on top of you. Careful." It cuts a lower-weight line in flight, a caution or flag call included; the meatball, the start lights, the restart green, a fuel-critical warning and the spotter's car-alongside calls keep the radio. No radio frame: the rejoin lines repeat while you stay stopped.
pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-right-behind.test: Harness → Traffic → Rejoin right behind. In-sim: stop on track in practice just as a car is about to reach you.

pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-near-first.comment: The first call about a car two to nine seconds away, one sentence in three pieces each picked from its pool: an intro that leads into the seconds, the seconds, and an outro, such as "Car coming in about five seconds. Watch out." It cuts a lower-weight line in flight, a caution or flag call included; the meatball, the start lights, the restart green, a fuel-critical warning and the spotter's car-alongside calls keep the radio. No radio frame.
pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-near-first.test: Harness → Traffic → Rejoin near, first call. In-sim: stop on track as a car is a few seconds away.

pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-near-update.comment: A later count of the same approach, each time its arrival has dropped by three seconds or more: an update intro that leads into the seconds, and the seconds, such as "Getting closer, about five seconds." It cuts a lower-weight line in flight, a caution or flag call included; the meatball, the start lights, the restart green, a fuel-critical warning and the spotter's car-alongside calls keep the radio. No radio frame.
pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-near-update.test: Harness → Traffic → Rejoin near, count. In-sim: stay stopped on track while a car closes from about nine seconds away.

pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-over-ten.comment: Stopped or crawling on track with the nearest car ten to fifteen seconds away: a whole line from a pool of four, such as "Next car is more than ten seconds away. Be careful." or "Next car is over ten seconds back." No radio frame.
pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-over-ten.test: Harness → Traffic → Rejoin over ten. In-sim: stop on track with the nearest car a little over ten seconds away.

pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-clear.comment: Stopped or crawling on track with no car within fifteen seconds: a whole line from a pool of four, such as "Clear to rejoin." or "Nothing close. Clear to rejoin." No radio frame.
pit-crew.traffic-rejoin-clear.test: Harness → Traffic → Rejoin clear. In-sim: stop on track in practice with no car close behind.

pit-crew.traffic-pit-exit-traffic.comment: As you leave your pit box, a car on track is predicted at the end of the exit blend line around the same time as you: a line from a pool of four, such as "We're estimating traffic at the pit exit. Watch out." or "Looks like traffic at the pit exit. Careful." It cuts a lower-weight line in flight, a caution or flag call included, so the exit readback and the tire-wear report play after it; the meatball, the start lights, the restart green, a fuel-critical warning and the spotter's car-alongside calls keep the radio.
pit-crew.traffic-pit-exit-traffic.test: Harness → Traffic → Pit exit traffic. In-sim: leave your pit box with a car on track about to pass the pit exit.

pit-crew.traffic-pit-exit-clear.comment: As you leave your pit box with no car predicted at the end of the exit blend line around the same time as you: a line from a pool of four, such as "Looks like the pit exit will be clear." or "Pit exit should be clear." It cuts a lower-weight line in flight, so the exit readback and the tire-wear report play after it; a caution or flag call, the meatball, the start lights, a fuel-critical warning and the spotter keep the radio.
pit-crew.traffic-pit-exit-clear.test: Harness → Traffic → Pit exit clear. In-sim: leave your pit box with no car near the pit exit.

pit-crew.fastest-lap-race.comment: The race's fastest lap is set — says who set it (you, the leader, the car ahead or behind, or another car by number and position) in one sentence-final clip, then the lap time to the thousandth as whole phrases, the minute and seconds clock followed by the thousandths, the way every lap is read, then, after a short pause, the gap to the tenth when there is one (the thousandths end the time, so the two are never joined).
pit-crew.fastest-lap-race.test: Harness → Fastest Lap → Yours (Taken from you, Leader, Car ahead, Car behind, Other car for the other lines; Yours in the grace plays the best-lap line). In-sim: an offline AI race; set the fastest lap of the race from lap 3 on, or let an AI car beat it.

pit-crew.sector-comparison-leader.comment: Pace check against the class leader at the line, after the lap time: how much quicker the leader is over a lap and where most of it is lost (or that we're slower in every sector), with the sector where we're quicker; or that we're quicker than the leader, with the sector where they're quicker.
pit-crew.sector-comparison-leader.test: Harness → Sectors → Leader pace, most of it with a gain (Leader pace, the most; Leader pace, every sector; Quicker than the leader). In-sim: an offline AI race at a track with three or more sectors; run three clean laps and cross the line from lap 4 on.

pit-crew.sector-comparison-ahead.comment: The car ahead by number and the sector where it is slower than us, at the line after the lap time.
pit-crew.sector-comparison-ahead.test: Harness → Sectors → Chance on the car ahead. In-sim: an offline AI race; close to within three seconds of a car that is slow through one sector and cross the line on a clean lap.

pit-crew.sector-comparison-behind.comment: The car behind by number and the sector where it is quicker than us, at the line after the lap time.
pit-crew.sector-comparison-behind.test: Harness → Sectors → Car behind quicker. In-sim: an offline AI race; let a car that is quick through one sector close to within three seconds and cross the line on a clean lap.

pit-crew.lap-time-last.comment: Every lap that is not a new best: a short sentence-final intro, then the lap time read as whole phrases, the minute and seconds as one clip and the thousandths as another (one twenty three, point four five six).
pit-crew.lap-time-last.test: Harness → Lap Time → Every lap 1:45.237 (Every lap under a minute 58.041; Out lap — silent). In-sim: any session; complete a lap that is not a new best.

radio.comment: The walkie-talkie frame: an open tick, the pit-lane ambience bed, a close tick. A line ended mid-word (its condition stopped being true) is abandoned with a short never-mind and the same close.

readback-body.comment: The service recap both readbacks share: fuel, tires or compound, a beat, then fast repair and windshield only when there is something to say. Each slot is a whole clause, so a slot that resolves to nothing leaves a shorter recap that is still true.

gap-readout.comment: The live gap readout both gap lines share: "Gap is", the whole seconds, the tenths. One optional clause, not three optional steps — the three vars resolve on a single check (the gap is readable, under a minute, and still to the car the line named), so the readout is spoken whole or left out whole, and the line before it is a complete sentence either way.
